_comment: MANIFEST-style expected fire/no-fire fixture for the Pillar 3 (Blast Radius) corpus under testdata/c/blast_radius_examples.c and testdata/sql/schema.sql. Consumed by tests/golden/test_blast_radius_golden.py. overflow_sign: 1 = must fire (overflow_bytes > 0), 0 = must NOT fire (no BlastRadiusFinding at all).

c.name: signature
c.scenario: RSA-2048 signature (256B classically) vs ML-DSA-65 signature (3309B)

c.name: pubkey
c.scenario: Ed25519 public key (32B classically) vs ML-DSA-65 public key (1952B)

c.name: rsa_signature_buf
c.scenario: generously-sized buffer, fits ML-DSA-65's signature (3309B) easily

sql.name: signature
sql.scenario: VARCHAR(512) signature column vs ML-DSA-65 signature (3309B), via the db_column name-pattern-only fallback

python.name: signature_buf
python.scenario: RSA-2048 signature (256B classically, jwt.encode(algorithm='RS256')) vs ML-DSA-65 signature (3309B) -- NAME-PATTERN correlation ('signature_buf' matches the 'signature' name pattern directly)

python.name: outbox
python.scenario: same RSA-2048 signature, but the 512-byte buffer name ('outbox') matches no name pattern -- correlated purely via DATA-FLOW (outbox[:len(signature)] = signature) -- must still fire since 512B < ML-DSA-65's 3309B

python.name: reply
python.scenario: same DATA-FLOW correlation as 'outbox', but generously sized at 8192B -- even ML-DSA-65's 3309B signature fits, so this must NOT fire
